summary.text: Regina Boyce is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 43A and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She advanced from the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026, alongside fellow incumbent Elizabeth Embry.
Her pre-legislative career included work in the Baltimore City Council President's office and at Strong City Baltimore.

paragraphs.text: Regina Boyce was born in Washington, D.C., and graduated from Woodlawn High School in 1994.
Boyce earned a B.S. in kinesiology and psychology from Towson University in 1998 and a master of public administration from the University of Baltimore in 2014.
She worked in the Department of Athletics and Recreation at Johns Hopkins University from 2000 to 2010, according to her legislative biography.

From 2010 to 2015 Boyce worked in the office of the Baltimore City Council President, first as a community liaison for North and Northeast Baltimore and then as deputy director of neighborhood relations.
She then worked at Strong City Baltimore as director of community services from 2015 to 2017 and as director of its Adult Learning Center from 2017 to 2019.
Ballotpedia also lists Boyce as a past president and vice president of the board of directors of Waverly Main Street.

In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for District 43A, Boyce received 9,837 votes (51.3%) to fellow incumbent Elizabeth Embry's 9,339 (48.7%), and both advanced to the general election for the district's two seats.
The General Assembly website lists Boyce as a member of the Environment and Transportation Committee.
